author: projectsagana
text:
As I see the forum post, the Diamond is being posted as continuation pattern and reversal pattern.

Which is it?

From what I understand big players confuse novice traders in attempt to fill their big orders as much as possible, so diamonds appear at HTF supply and demand and we can expect a trend reversal. So only when price action has clearly changed its direction we can take advantage of this pattern at the retest.

So a diamond shaped price action that did not reversed its trend is not technically RTM's Diamond trade set up until it the trend has reversed.

Some one help me clear this one as I want to practice my eyes for the right patterns

Thanks

At first I didn't understand the value of the diamond, either. How can it be traded? The answer is in here - in IF's first post, and a post by Kruger. Firstly, it's dangerous, and is like a failed QM, so as per IF we need to be absolutely sure about where to put our stops - outside of the fakeout zone. As per Kruger, we don't trade the diamond as such, but look to enter on the return to the diamond. A diamond is a fight that draws in a crowd (suckers, like me) and then everyone gets spat out. Nasty. However, what the diamond also is (at least appears to be) is a very strong Flag/RBD/DBR. There's some big action out of these, and that's what we can look to take advantage of. I spotted this todat on a chart I was checking out for Lupy, on a failed flag trade. readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/journa...lupy-s-journal#29540

I looked in further then the M5 and I found this little diamond.

it was a valid QM that worked till its first target, what happened after that doesnt count as a failed QM or a DM (a DM should have engulfed the HH)

price breaking the QM level doesnt mean the QM failed either

the diamond in general is a hard one to trade on itself without factoring in other things. in any case its designed to play with your psychology and throw you off. you can worry about these later. anyway, looks like you do a good start in your studies, keep working and i bet you will do well
